**Deal notes added by Sofia Bergström 2026-09-21:**
Kärnhuset is back, and this time with a customer and a date. The foodservice group's tender, page 41: product level figures for all products offered, documented method, share of primary data stated, zero points on criterion 4.3 (10% of the evaluation) without them. Submission 15 January, noon. The category director presented it at a supplier day in May that their commercial director attended and did not mention.

Madeleine had read our scorecard blog post and used it as a checklist against the tender: date, named person, consequence. All three.

I re-sent the customer scorecard framing. She had read the note at the top in August ("works best when you can name a customer and a date") and correctly didn't use it then. This time it fits.

New scope: 62 products from two of four entities (bakery, ready meals), corporate footprint from the same model, no supplier data yet. Gustav wants it under 25k, the board threshold. One page business case, his own sentence at the top: "we score zero on ten percent of a tender worth eight percent of our revenue." Risks: recipes in a 2014 system one person (Kent, retiring March) can open, Madeleine's time (Gustav naming someone from the ready meals entity), and unknown scoring of a low primary data share (ask in the clarification round, open until end of October).

Gustav decides by 9 October. Madeleine is staying until January for this.

Lesson for the notes from the loss: the board said no to a regulation. The CFO says yes to arithmetic.
